title: CCIP USDC Bridge
description: Moves USDC from the Avalanche C-Chain to Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base or OP testnets over Chainlink CCIP. A small transferor contract adds a destination allowlist, fee quoting, and native-fee refunds on top of the CCIP router.
prompts: Send USDC from Avalanche to Base
Bridge USDC from the C-Chain to Ethereum with Chainlink CCIP
Let users move stablecoins from Avalanche to other EVM chains

source.description: Avalanche chain the USDC leaves from

destination.description: EVM chain the USDC arrives on

params.name: owner
params.description: Manages allowed destinations and recovers stuck funds

params.name: receiver
params.description: Receives the USDC on the destination chain

params.name: amount
params.description: USDC to send, in 6-decimal base units; the default is 0.5 USDC

prerequisites: USDC on Fuji from the Circle faucet listed in the registry
Fuji AVAX for gas and the CCIP fee (fees are paid in native AVAX by default)
Nothing is deployed on the destination: USDC arrives straight in the receiver's wallet

contracts.name: ERC20
contracts.description: Standard ERC-20 ABI, for USDC approvals and balances

steps.title: Deploy the transferor on the C-Chain
Transfer the transferor to its owner
Quote the CCIP fee in native AVAX

checks.description: The receiver holds USDC on the destination chain

review: The router and chain selectors come from the registry; USDC is in the lane's transferableTokens for both chains.
extraArgs is a call argument encoded off-chain for the lane (V3 on CCIP 2.0 lanes), never a constant in the contract.
The native fee is quoted with getFee right before sending; any excess msg.value is refunded to the caller.
Only allowlisted destination chains can be used, and the owner is the builder.

frontend.summary: Move USDC from Avalanche to another chain: choose where, enter an amount, see the fee, send, and see it arrive.
audience: USDC holders moving funds between Avalanche and other chains
journeys: Choose the destination by chain name; only destinations this bridge supports appear.
Enter an amount next to 'You have 120.00 USDC' with a Max button, and see the fee in AVAX and what arrives before signing.
Send in two visible steps (1 of 2: allow USDC, 2 of 2: bridge), skipping the first when the allowance already covers it.
Track arrival with an honest estimate (minutes between most lanes, 20 minutes or more from Ethereum testnets), and confirm with the new balance on the destination.
When the wallet has no USDC or AVAX, say so and link the Builder Hub faucet (https://build.avax.network/console/primary-network/faucet).
flows: Check router.isChainSupported(selector) and show only destinations that are allowlisted on the transferor.
Encode extraArgs with @chainlink/ccip-sdk for the chosen lane, quote getFee(...), and show the fee in AVAX before the user signs.
Approve exactly the USDC amount, then call transferTokens with the quoted fee as value; read messageId from TokensTransferred.
Track the message on https://ccip.chain.link and poll the receiver's USDC balance on the destination; Ethereum-based testnets can take 20 minutes or more.
